title: Actium
objective: After this level you can explain the Battle of Actium and its consequences.
summary: In 31 BCE Agrippa’s fleet beat Antony and Cleopatra at Actium. Both died in 30 BCE, Egypt became Roman, and Octavian stood alone.

cards.headline: One sea battle decided who would rule the Roman world.
War on a queen
cards.body: In 32 BCE Rome declared war on Cleopatra, not on Antony, so the conflict looked like a foreign war rather than another civil war. Octavian’s closest friend, Marcus Agrippa, was his leading general and admiral, and commanded his fleet.

cards.headline: The battle
cards.body: On 2 September 31 BCE, Octavian’s fleet defeated Antony and Cleopatra at Actium, off western Greece. The next year, as Octavian took Alexandria, Antony and Cleopatra both took their own lives.

cards.headline: Master of the Roman world
cards.body: Egypt became a Roman province under Octavian’s personal control, and its grain helped feed Rome. After Actium, one man stood alone at the top of the Roman world.

cards.headline: Actium: decided
learned: Agrippa won at Actium in 31 BCE
Antony and Cleopatra died in 30 BCE

questions.prompt: Who commanded Octavian’s fleet at Actium?

options.label: Mark Antony
options.rationale: He was on the other side.

questions.explanation: Agrippa, Octavian’s closest friend, commanded his fleet.

questions.prompt: Why did Rome declare war on Cleopatra rather than on Antony?

options.label: To make it look like a foreign war

questions.explanation: A war against a foreign queen was easier to rally Romans behind than one more civil war.

questions.prompt: From Level 42: what had Antony done that let Octavian call him a traitor?

options.label: Surrendered his legions to the Parthians
Killed Octavian’s sister
options.rationale: He left her; he didn’t kill her.

options.label: Given Roman lands to Cleopatra and her children

questions.explanation: The Donations of Alexandria handed Roman territory to Cleopatra’s family.
